title: Creamy White Bean Carbonara (CarBEANara)
ingredients: 4 ounces (113 g) guanciale, pancetta, or bacon, cut into 1/4-inch pieces (about 3/4 cup); see notes
3 (15-ounce, 425 g each) cans cannellini beans, undrained
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus more as needed
1 1/4 teaspoons freshly ground black pepper, plus more for garnish
1/2 teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume
4 ounces (113 g) grated Pecorino Romano cheese (about 1 cup), divided
steps: In a large skillet, cook guanciale, pancetta, or bacon over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until fat is rendered and meat is browned and crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer to a paper towel–lined plate, leaving drippings in skillet.

Meanwhile, pour beans through a fine-mesh strainer set over a large bowl; reserve bean liquid. Add beans, 1/2 cup reserved bean liquid, and 1/2 cup water to drippings in the skillet. (Discard or reserve remaining bean liquid for another use.) Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until beans are heated through and liquid is slightly thickened, 3 to 5 minutes.

While beans cook, in a medium bowl, whisk together egg yolks, egg, pepper, salt, and 3 ounces (about 3/4 cup) of the Pecorino Romano until smooth. Gradually spoon 5 tablespoons (1 tablespoon at a time) of the hot liquid from skillet into egg mixture, whisking constantly, until slightly loosened. Whisk 1/4 cup beans with their liquid into egg mixture until loosened and warmed. Remove skillet from heat.

Gradually pour egg mixture into beans in skillet, stirring constantly, until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth, glossy, and creamy, about 1 minute. If needed, stir in more water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until sauce reaches desired consistency.
Divide bean mixture evenly among 4 bowls. Sprinkle evenly with reserved crisped meat and remaining 1 ounce Pecorino Romano. Garnish with black pepper. Serve immediately with crusty bread.
notes:
Guanciale, cured pork jowl, is generally considered the most authentic choice for classic pasta carbonara; it’s fattier than pancetta or bacon and often more heavily spiced, creating a dish with pronounced spice notes and an extra-unctuous texture. Pancetta delivers the cleanest porky flavor, while American bacon, though less traditional, adds a hit of pleasant smoke. Use whichever you prefer for this bean dish.
This dish is best eaten right away, but leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
Reheat gently in a skillet over low heat, stirring frequently and adding water 1 tablespoon at a time as needed to loosen the sauce.
